actionable.finding: renderNotificationCenter interpolated emailAttempts into HTML without escaping.
actionable.reachability: Built-in SQLite schema enforces numeric attempts and jobs write numeric counts. Exported renderer and custom NotificationClient accept runtime JavaScript or unvalidated response data that can supply markup; mountNotificationCenter assigns the result to innerHTML.
actionable.fix: Escape emailAttempts using the same HTML encoder as the remaining dynamic text.
actionable.baseline: d6baafc renderer has no email-attempt markup; preceding id/title/body/url values are escaped.
actionable.regression: tests/notifications.test.mjs: notification rendering escapes malformed attempt counts from custom clients
actionable.verification: Source-only exact renderer extraction via native TypeScript stripping passed on Node 24: malicious img/onerror markup escaped and numeric rendering preserved. No dist writes; rebuilt suite delegated to root final matrix.

nonActionable.reason: Both finally blocks execute after awaiting flight and clear the shared in-flight slot only if it still references the same Promise. Awaiting the compared values would compare resolutions instead of identities and break deduplication cleanup.
A doesNotMatch assertion checks a fixed lowercase script payload. Production renderer escapes angle brackets without relying on tag case or this regex.

Only internal stable/candidate label literals reach JSON.stringify. It emits a quoted JavaScript string in a Node .mjs file, not HTML; no untrusted caller or script-element terminator boundary exists.
domains assignment already exists at d6baafc:1358. No security boundary change. Generated copies repeat the same finding.
Valid compact JavaScript in tests; no production execution or escaping issue.

preservedOutOfScope.reason: Preexisting untracked user verification script; preserved without edits. Parent responsible for remaining scan scope.

conclusion: One introduced production-library escaping gap fixed with a regression. No additional actionable CodeQL finding in the owned source modules. This triage does not claim that a clean static scan proves absence of vulnerabilities.
